newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says new chicken disease a false alarm.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says new chicken disease a false alarm.

text.p: Taiwan's Council of Agriculture said on Thursday a suspected outbreak of a deadly chicken epidemic was a false alarm.
It assured local residents that there was no problem with the island's 118 million chickens and that the poultry was safe to eat.

Council official Chen Jung-jang told Reuters test results showed that the chickens did not die of the "New Castle" disease -- a type of deadly and highly contagious disease, commonly known as chicken plague.
The council's initial finding showed it was an isolated case and that the disease was not highly contagious, Chen said. He said the council had yet to determine the cause of the disease.
"It (the unknown one) may cause some deaths, but it would not affect our large chicken population," he said.
Local media had earlier speculated the island's chickens were infected with the "New Castle" disease, which would force mass slaughter to prevent the epidemic from spreading.
Chen said the council began investigating on Tuesday when a chicken farmer in Taiwan's southern county of Tainan reported a few thousand of his 50,000 chickens had died.
Taiwan has about 118 million chickens, raised mostly for domestic consumption.

Fears of a disease outbreak caused Taiwan's food related stock shares to fall 1.29 percent on Thursday. Major chicken breeding firms Great Wall Enterprise and Charoen Pokphand fell by the daily seven percent limit to T$27.00 and T$28.50 respectively.
